item.title: Tibiofemoral AP / PA Mobilization
patientPosition: Supine with knee supported in a comfortable flexed or near-extended position depending on target motion.
therapistPosition: Stand beside the knee with hands close to the joint line.
stabilization: Stabilize femur while mobilizing tibia or stabilize tibia while mobilizing femur according to chosen glide.
contact: Broad contact over proximal tibia, avoiding fibular head/peroneal nerve compression.
forceDirection: AP or PA glide selected from target movement and response.
Use small amplitude for pain, larger amplitude into resistance for stiffness.
mistakes: Not linking mobility gain to exercise.
safety: Avoid with fracture, acute ligamentous instability, infection, DVT or immediately post-op without clearance.
item.visualCue: Femur stable ↔ Tibia glides AP/PA → Re-test knee ROM/function.

subTechniques.name: Posterior Tibial Glide for Knee Flexion
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve knee flexion when posterior tibial glide is restricted and the treatment changes the comparable sign.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the knee flexed to a comfortable angle and the foot supported.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the distal femur and use a broad contact over the proximal tibia, avoiding fibular-head nerve compression.
subTechniques.direction: Glide the tibia posteriorly on the femur with the selected oscillatory grade.
subTechniques.reassess: Knee flexion, squat and stair descent.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Match the glide to the motion you are trying to improve; for open-chain tibial flexion, the concave tibia glides posteriorly.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute instability, fracture, DVT or uncleared postoperative restriction.

subTechniques.name: Anterior Tibial Glide for Knee Extension
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve terminal extension when anterior tibial glide is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the knee near extension and comfortably supported.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the femur and contact the proximal posterior tibia broadly while protecting the popliteal region.
subTechniques.direction: Glide the tibia anteriorly relative to the femur with a low-to-moderate oscillatory grade.
subTechniques.reassess: Terminal knee extension, gait and step-down.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Do not push directly into the popliteal fossa; use broad proximal-tibial control.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid acute posterior knee pathology or vascular concerns.

subTechniques.name: Patellar Inferior Glide
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve knee flexion when inferior patellar mobility is a relevant limiter.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the quadriceps relaxed and knee supported in slight flexion.
subTechniques.contact: Use both thumbs or broad finger pads on the superior patellar border without compressing the tendon.
subTechniques.direction: Translate the patella inferiorly in a smooth oscillatory or sustained manner.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: A relaxed quadriceps makes patellar mobility easier to assess and treat.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Respect recent surgery and acute patellofemoral irritation.
